text:
### Observed differences

- Six activities became near-universal in the later window: A28, A30 and A31 each ran in about 49 in 100 traces before and about 99 in 100 after; A32, A33 and A34 each ran in about 52 in 100 before and in all but about 1 in 200 traces after. Each activity still occurs at most once per trace in both windows. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- Before, the two triads were mutually exclusive alternatives: no trace contained both a member of {A28, A30, A31} and a member of {A32, A33, A34} (co-occurrence 0 in 200 traces), while about 49 in 100 traces contained all of the first triad and about 52 in 100 all of the second. In the later window, every cross-triad pair co-occurs in about 98 in 100 traces, always with the {A28, A30, A31} member first. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024]
- Order within each triad stays unfixed in both windows: for example, A28 precedes A30 in about 49 in 100 and follows it in about 50 in 100 of the later traces, and the same two-way pattern holds for A28/A31, A30/A31 and within {A32, A33, A34}. [REL013, REL014, REL018, REL025, REL026, REL027]
- A25 and A26 occur in every trace in both windows and bracket the block: A25 precedes each of the six activities in about 99 in 100 later traces (earlier it preceded whichever triad ran), and each of the six precedes A26. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- Successor profiles agree: before, A25's outgoing transitions spread roughly evenly over all six activities (about 15–19 in 100 each); in the later window, about 99 in 100 go to A28, A30 or A31. Before, A28, A30 and A31 each led to A26 in about 30–36 in 100 of their outgoing transitions; in the later window almost never (about 1 in 200), with the remainder split between their triad partners and A32/A33/A34. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- Event distances match one triad being inserted after the other: the gap from A25 to A32/A33/A34 and from A28/A30/A31 to A26 moved from 1–3 event positions before to 4–5 positions in the later window. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]
- Relative event positions shifted accordingly: A28/A30/A31 occur earlier (mean position about 0.74 before, 0.68 after) and A32/A33/A34 later (about 0.73 before, 0.77 after); A25 moved slightly earlier (0.67 to 0.62) and A26 slightly later (0.80 to 0.83). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that two alternative blocks were combined into a single sequence: before, a case executed either {A28, A30, A31} or {A32, A33, A34} — roughly half of cases each, never both — between the always-present A25 and A26; in the later window, nearly every case executes both triads in sequence, first {A28, A30, A31} in no fixed internal order, then {A32, A33, A34} in no fixed internal order. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, OCC001, OCC004]

The support is direct and consistent: the cross-triad relation changed from never co-occurring to co-occurring in about 98 in 100 traces with a fixed order between the triads, participation of all six activities rose to near 1, and the successor, distance and position indicators all match the picture of one triad being inserted after the other. The screening volume (51 qualifying items against about 0.6 expected for an unchanged process) is far above what chance produces. The agreeing indicators largely describe the same trace behaviour, so they corroborate but are not independent confirmations. [REL015, DIR001, LAG001, POS003, POS006]

Limitations: with 200 traces per window, the evidence cannot exclude that combined cases existed before but were too rare to appear (the change would then be a rare variant becoming dominant rather than a routing change affecting all cases), and a small share of later cases still skips individual activities (participation 98.5–99.5 in 100), so it is unclear whether the combined sequence is fully mandatory. The evidence shows the behavioural outcome, not the mechanism behind it. [REL015, OCC001, OCC004]

Other differences: minor residuals remain in the later window — A25 still leads directly to A32 or A34 in about 1–2 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, and A28 leads to A26 in about 1 in 200 traces — small exceptions to the otherwise clean block sequence. [DIR001, DIR002]
